intro: Toyota Japan's maintenance booklet isn't online, so this is a suggested UK-owner schedule. The fluids and capacities come from the owner's manual; the intervals are common practice and are marked unverified until checked against the Japanese メンテナンスノート. Use 'severe' if most of your driving is short trips, towing, or heavy loads.

items.note: Many UK owners change it every 6,000 miles or yearly, whichever comes first.
Toyota Japan allows every second oil change. Changing it every time is cheap insurance.
Japan's shaken inspection cycle and normal UK garage practice.
Toyota's usual Super LLC interval is 160,000 km for the first change, then every 80,000 km. On an import of unknown history, change it once and start counting.
The rear bank needs the intake plenum off, so it's a bigger job.

Toyota says 'consult a dealer' and lists no interval. Japanese garages recommend changing it to prevent judder; plenty of cars reach 150,000 km never having had it changed. On a high-mileage car with old fluid, change it gradually (a drain & fill at a time).
Sealed 'lifetime' fill. Owners do a drain & fill as preventive maintenance.
Dry runners make the power doors labour and wear the cables.
Or as soon as the key's range drops.
A UK legal requirement once the car is 3 years old.
